enonce.question: Complete: Yesterday I ___ (visit) my grandmother.

Look at the information about three pupils.
| Name | Height | Age |
|---|---|---|
| Hamza | $160\ \text{cm}$ | 14 |
| Bassem | $152\ \text{cm}$ | 13 |
| Rayen | $145\ \text{cm}$ | 12 |

1) Write the comparative form of: tall, short, old, young.
2) Complete: Hamza is ______ than Bassem. (tall)
3) Complete: Rayen is ______ than Bassem. (short)
4) Write one sentence to compare Hamza's age and Rayen's age.
Past of "go".

Read the dialogue between two friends on Monday morning.
Walid: (you / play) tennis yesterday?
Skander: Yes, I did. I played with my cousin.
Walid: (you / win) the match?
Skander: No, I didn't. My cousin won.
Walid: (your father / watch) the match?
Skander: Yes, he did.

1) Write Walid's three questions in the past simple.
2) Complete the rule: Did + subject + ______ verb.
3) Write the two short answers to: Did you play tennis yesterday?

Read what Dorra did last Saturday.
Last Saturday, Dorra went to the cinema with her cousin. She saw a funny film. After the film, they ate a pizza.
Her brother Aziz stayed at home, so his Saturday was different.

1) Make the sentence negative: She saw the film.
2) Write two negative sentences about Aziz: He went to the cinema. / He ate a pizza.
3) Complete the rule: did not (didn't) + ______ verb.
4) Give the base form of: saw, went, ate.

Read the facts about two Tunisian cities.
| City | Size | Summer weather |
|---|---|---|
| Tunis | very big | hot |
| Tozeur | small | very hot |

1) Write the comparative of big and hot. What happens to the last consonant?
2) Complete: Tunis is ______ than Tozeur. (big)
3) Complete: In summer, Tozeur is ______ than Tunis. (hot)
4) Write the comparative of thin and small. Which one doubles the consonant?

Read about two days in Lotfi's week.
On Monday, Lotfi had a difficult Maths test. He was not very happy. On Friday, he had an easy English test and then a party with funny games. It was a very happy day.

1) Write the comparative of happy. What happens to the y?
2) Complete: Lotfi was ______ on Friday than on Monday. (happy)
3) Complete: The English test was ______ than the Maths test. (easy)
4) Write the comparative of: funny, busy.

Look at the table.
| Transport | Speed | Price |
|---|---|---|
| bike | slow | cheap |
| car | fast | expensive |

1) Complete: A car is ______ (fast) than a bike.
2) Complete: A bike is ______ (slow) than a car, but it is ______ (cheap).
3) Complete with two words: A car is ______ ______ (expensive) than a bike.
4) Which small word comes after the comparative in these sentences?
Complete: This book is ___ (interesting) than that one.
Comparative of "good".

Read the paragraph.
My favourite season is summer. In summer, the weather is hot and sunny. I go to the beach with my family and I swim every day. I also eat a lot of ice cream. That is why I love summer.

1) Copy the first sentence of the paragraph. What is the paragraph about?
2) Choose: the first sentence gives (a detail / the main idea) of the paragraph. It is called the ______ sentence.
3) Choose the best first sentence for a paragraph about a best friend: a) He has a blue bike. b) My best friend is Aymen. c) We play football on Sundays.
What are the three parts of a paragraph?

Read Islem's sentences. He forgot the punctuation mark at the end of each one.
a) My name is Islem
b) I live in Monastir
c) Where do you live
d) I have two brothers

1) Which punctuation mark ends a statement (a sentence that gives information)? Write its name and its sign.
2) Add the right punctuation mark at the end of the four sentences.
3) Does every sentence begin with a small letter or a capital letter?

Read the paragraph about Marwa's hobby.
I love cooking. I make cakes at the weekend and I help my mother in the kitchen. I also watch cooking programmes on TV. My sister likes cooking too.

1) Find three linking words in the text that add an idea.
2) Join the two sentences with and: I play the guitar. I sing.
3) Add the word also in the right place: I like football. I like tennis.
4) Write two sentences about your free time and link them with a word that adds an idea.

Read the paragraph. Its first sentence is missing.
______ It is near the sea and it has a beautiful old medina. There are many shops, cafés and gardens. The streets are always full of people. That is why I love living in Sousse.

1) Choose the best topic sentence: a) There is a big market on Sundays. b) Sousse is a beautiful and lively city. c) I go to school by bus.
2) Why are the two other sentences not good topic sentences?
3) Now write a topic sentence for a paragraph about your own city or village.

Read the paragraph about two brothers.
Slim and Fedi are brothers, but they are very different. Slim likes sport. However, Fedi prefers reading. Slim is tall, but Fedi is short.

1) Find the two linking words that show contrast (a difference between two ideas).
2) Join the two sentences with but: I like tea. I don't like coffee.
3) Choose the right connector: It was cold, (and / but / because) we went to the beach.
4) Write one sentence with but about you and a friend.
Correct capitalization: my friend lives in tunis.
Order: concluding sentence, topic sentence, supporting sentences.
Write a short concluding sentence for a paragraph about school.

Compare the two texts.
Text A: I got up late. I missed the bus. I walked to school. I was tired. I was happy. I arrived on time.
Text B: I got up late, so I missed the bus. Then I walked to school. I was tired, but I was happy because I arrived on time.

1) Find the four linking words in text B.
2) Which text is easier and nicer to read? Why?
3) What does each linking word show: a result, an order in time, a contrast or a reason?
4) Join with a linking word: It was raining. I took my umbrella.
Order (most to least): never, always, sometimes, often.
Complete: He ___ (100%) does his homework.

Read about Nesrine's habits.
| Activity | How often? |
|---|---|
| get up early | always |
| be late for school | never |
| help her mother | often |

Nesrine says: I get up early. I am late for school. I help my mother.

1) Put the adverb in the right place: I get up early. (always)
2) Do the same with: I am late for school. (never) / I help my mother. (often)
3) Complete the rule: the adverb goes ______ the main verb, but ______ the verb to be.
Complete: We ___ (usually) have lunch at noon.
Place the adverb with "be": She (often) is late.

Sofiene writes about his school days, but the adverbs are in the wrong place.
a) I go always to school by bus.
b) My friends are late never.
c) We play sometimes football after school.

1) Find the adverb of frequency in each sentence.
2) Rewrite the three sentences with the adverb in the correct place.
3) Ask Sofiene a question about sentence c). Begin with How often ...?
Complete: They ___ (0%) eat meat (they are vegetarians).
Ask about frequency: (you / go) to the cinema?
Rewrite with an adverb: I watch TV every day.
Write a sentence about your routine with an adverb of frequency.
Countable or uncountable: water.

Look at the food on the kitchen table: an apple, some milk, three eggs, some rice, two tomatoes, some sugar.

1) Is apple countable or uncountable? Write its plural.
2) Put the six nouns in two groups: countable / uncountable.
3) Complete with a, an or some: ______ egg, ______ rice, ______ tomato.
4) Choose: we can put a number before (countable / uncountable) nouns.

Hichem is preparing a picnic basket.
In my basket, I have ______ bread, ______ apple, ______ cheese, ______ banana and ______ water.

1) Complete the text with a, an or some.
2) Put the five nouns in two groups: countable / uncountable.
3) Choose the correct sentence: I have a bread. / I have some bread.
4) We can count bread with a special word. Complete: a ______ of bread.

Mum and Sonia are preparing a cake.
Mum: Is there ______ milk in the fridge?
Sonia: Yes, there is ______ milk, but there isn't ______ butter.
Mum: Are there ______ eggs?
Sonia: Yes, there are ______ eggs on the table.

1) Complete the dialogue with some or any.
2) Complete the rule: we use ______ in affirmative sentences, and ______ in negative sentences and questions.
3) Write a question with any about sugar.

The librarian is counting the things in the school library.
| Thing | Number |
|---|---|
| books | 850 |
| computers | 6 |
| chairs | 40 |

1) Choose the right word: How (much / many) books are there in the library?
2) Answer question 1 with a full sentence.
3) Write a question with How many about the computers and answer it.
4) Choose: “How many” is used with (countable plural / uncountable) nouns.

Mrs Dridi is making tea and cakes for her guests. Her daughter helps her.
Daughter: How ______ sugar do you need, Mum?
Mrs Dridi: Two spoons, please. And how ______ flour do we have?
Daughter: One kilo.
Mrs Dridi: How ______ milk is there in the bottle?
Daughter: Not much.

1) Complete the three questions with much or many.
2) Are sugar, flour and milk countable or uncountable?
3) Use the words to write a question with How much: (water / you / drink / every day).

It is 7:50. School starts at 8:00 and Ghassen is still at home.
Mother: Hurry up, Ghassen! There isn't ______ time.
Ghassen: I know! Are there ______ pupils at the bus stop?
Mother: No, there aren't ______ pupils now. And there isn't ______ milk in your glass, so drink it quickly!

1) Complete the dialogue with much or many.
2) Explain your answer for “time” and for “pupils”.
3) Rewrite with much or many: I don't have a lot of money. / She doesn't have a lot of friends.

Look at these quantity expressions: a bottle of ... / a glass of ... / a piece of ... / a cup of ... / a kilo of ...

1) Give two expressions from the list that go with water.
2) Match each of the three other expressions with one word: cake / tea / rice.
3) Why can't we say “two waters” in the same way as “two apples”?
4) Rewrite correctly, using the word glass: I drink three waters every day.
Why can't we say "two milks"?
Correct: I have many money.
Complete (plan): I ___ (visit) Paris next summer.

Read Khalil's message to his friend. There are three mistakes after will.
Hi Ahmed! I am busy now, but I will to call you tonight. My brother wills bring your book tomorrow. Don't worry, we will helping you with the Maths homework.

1) Find the three mistakes.
2) Rewrite the three sentences correctly.
3) Complete the rule: after will, we use the ______ verb, without to, without -s and without -ing.

Read the four short situations.
a) The phone is ringing. — I will answer it!
b) I think Tunisia will win the match tomorrow.
c) Don't worry, Mum. I will tidy my room, I promise.
d) Your bag is heavy. I will carry it for you.

1) Match each sentence (a–d) with its use: a prediction or opinion / a quick decision / a promise / an offer.
2) Complete the rule: will + ______ verb, the same for all subjects.
3) Write the short forms of: I will / will not.
4) Write one prediction about your future with I think ... will ...

Read what Asma says.
I have decided what to do this summer. In July, I am going to visit my aunt in Djerba. My brother is going to join a swimming club. We bought the bus tickets yesterday!
Look at the sky! There are big black clouds. It is going to rain.

1) Find the three verbs with “going to” in the text.
2) Which two sentences are plans decided before? Which sentence is a prediction from something we can see?
3) Complete the rule: be going to + ______ verb.
4) Write one sentence about your plan for next weekend.

Riadh's birthday party is on Saturday, but there are some problems: his friend Maha is ill and the weather is bad.

Make the sentences negative.
1) She will come.
2) They will play in the garden.
3) I will be late.
4) Write the short form of will not, then rewrite sentence 1 with it.

The Zouari family have decided to go to Paris in August. A neighbour asks about their plans.
| Plan | Decision |
|---|---|
| travel | by plane |
| stay | in a hotel |
| visit | the Eiffel Tower |

1) Write the neighbour's question about their plan: (they / travel) by plane?
2) Answer it with a short answer.
3) Write two more questions: (they / stay) in a hotel? — (Mrs Zouari / visit) the Eiffel Tower?
4) Why do we use “going to” here, and not “will”?
Complete (prediction): It ___ (rain) tomorrow.
Complete (offer): The bag is heavy. I ___ help you.
Write a sentence about your plan for the weekend.
Complete: Look at those clouds! It ___ rain. (evidence)

It is three o'clock in the afternoon at the Hammami family's house.
Look! The baby ______ (sleep) in his bed. Mother ______ (read) a book and the two boys ______ (play) chess. Listen! Father ______ (sing) in the kitchen.

1) Complete the text with the present continuous of the verbs in brackets.
2) Which two words in the text show that the actions are happening now?
3) Complete the rule: am / is / are + verb + ______.
Complete: I ___ (do) my homework at the moment.

Read the message.
Hi Rami! I am sitting in my room and I am ______ (write) an email to my pen friend. My sister is ______ (make) a cake and my father is ______ (drive) to the market. What are you doing?

1) Write the -ing form of the three verbs in brackets.
2) Which letter do these three verbs lose before -ing?
3) Write the -ing form of: come, dance, read.
4) Complete the rule: when a verb ends in a silent -e, we ______ the e and add -ing.

It is break time, but it is raining, so the pupils are inside.
| Who? | What are they doing now? |
|---|---|
| Ali and Samir | reading in the library |
| Nadia | talking to her friend |
| I | drawing |

1) Make the sentence negative: They are playing.
2) Write two negative sentences: Nadia (eat). / I (run).
3) Write the short forms of: are not / is not.
4) Write an affirmative sentence about Ali and Samir.

It is sports day at school.
Look at the pupils! Youssef is ______ (run) very fast. Two girls are ______ (swim) in the pool. Their friends are ______ (sit) on the grass and they are ______ (clap).

1) Write the -ing form of the four verbs in brackets.
2) What happens to the last letter of these verbs?
3) Write the -ing form of: play, stop, read.
4) Explain why we write running but playing.

Zeineb describes what is happening in the park, but she makes one mistake in each sentence.
a) He is play football now.
b) The children running at the moment.
c) Look! The dog is swiming in the lake.

1) Find the mistake in each sentence.
2) Rewrite the three sentences correctly.
3) Complete the rule: present continuous = am / is / are + ______.

Mother is on the phone with Grandma. Grandma asks about the family.
Grandma: Where is Imen? (she / read) now?
Mother: No, she isn't. She is doing her homework.
Grandma: And the boys? (they / watch) TV?
Mother: Yes, they are.
Grandma: (you / cook) dinner?
Mother: Yes, I am.

1) Write Grandma's three questions in the present continuous.
2) Complete the rule: Am / Is / Are + subject + verb + ______?
3) Give the two short answers to: Is she reading now?
What is the difference between present simple and present continuous?

Read the two short texts.
A. Mr Brahim is a baker. He gets up at four o'clock every day. He usually makes bread in the morning.
B. Today is Sunday. At the moment, Mr Brahim is not working. Look! He is playing with his children in the garden right now.

1) Find the time words or expressions in text B that go with the present continuous.
2) Find two time expressions in text A. Which tense goes with them?
3) Put the verb in the correct tense: Listen! The teacher ______ (speak). / She ______ (speak) English every day.
4) Give one more time word that goes with the present continuous.
Write a sentence about what you are doing now.
